page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. The compute setup comprises 32 shared vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Vector and tensor instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The instance is equipped with 384 GB of system RAM, allocating 12 GB per core, and incorporates two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S accelerators offering a combined 96 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier compute performance. The AMD EPYC processor scores in the top decile across stress-ng single-core (4,186.78) and multi-core (131,937.77) evaluations, matched by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 25,149.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 87,135.2. Synthetic memory testing yields solid throughput, including 327.05 GB/s uncached read bandwidth, while decompression throughput reaches 572.67 GB/s in multi-threaded bzip3. Database and key-value execution are also strong, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top 10% and Redis throughput reaching 127.0 million SET operations per second.

In AI inference workloads, the dual L40S GPUs deliver strong prompt and generation throughput on smaller architectures, achieving 5,508.2 prompt tokens per second and 360.16 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, alongside 220.88 prompt tokens per second on a 7B model. However, performance tapers into the middle tier on larger models, where 70B inference registers 21.91 prompt tokens per second and 4.14 generation tokens per second. An architectural tradeoff to note is the complete absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistent file operations.

Overall, the server provides substantial GPU and host compute density for high-throughput computing. It is well aligned for small-to-medium LLM inference, ray tracing, image and text processing pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory deployments, and data transformation tasks.
description: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a high-density GPU server built on KVM virtualization and x86_64 architecture. It features 32 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, 384 GB of system memory, and dual NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering 96 GB of total VRAM. Computational benchmarks show top-tier multi-core execution, reflected by high stress-ng and Geekbench scores, as well as rapid Redis throughput exceeding 127 million operations per second. Hardware acceleration enables top-tier inference speeds on lightweight neural models and strong output on 7B parameter models, though larger 70B models exhibit average throughput. Because local storage is not bundled, external block storage must be attached for operational persistence. The instance suits small to mid-scale LLM deployment, image processing, ray tracing, and intensive in-memory caching workflows.
